lines: Middle Eastern crisis 2026 Iran war 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis Iran's navy claims that an oil tanker caught on fire after hitting a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz. (Al Jazeera)
2026 Lebanon war The Israeli Air Force strikes a Hezbollah underground facility in Lebanon's Bekaa valley. (The Times of Israel)
Two Israeli drones explode in Nabatieh, Lebanon, without causing any injuries. (Al Jazeera)
Gaza war Gaza's health ministry reports that two people have been killed by recent Israeli attacks and two others died from their wounds over the past day. (Al Jazeera)

Yemeni civil war Houthi–Saudi conflict The Houthis fire missiles at King Abdullah Financial District in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which damage Public Investment Fund Tower and other buildings but cause no injuries. (Middle East Monitor) (Al-Monitor)

2026 Yemen offensives The Yemeni government's military claims to have killed or injured 144 Houthi fighters during recent operations in the Taiz, Marib, and Al-Jawf governorates, and to have repelled an attack in the Tur Al Bahah area. (Al Jazeera)
The Houthis claim that Saudi-led coalition airstrikes have killed 10 people in Sanaa, Yemen, over the past two days. (Al Jazeera)

In Bangladesh, banned Awami League members loot and burn properties in Gopalganj District, including BNP MP Md. Selimuzzaman Mollah's ancestral home, a police station, and a Grameen Bank branch, and vandalise BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami properties. Separately, attackers burn the homes of former politicians Rahim Ullah in Feni District, Shahriar Alam in Rajshahi District and Mahmud Hasan Sumon in Mymensingh District. (BSS) (The Financial Express) (The Business Standard in Bengali) (NTV in Bengali)

Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war The Joint Organisations Data Initiative reports that Saudi Arabia's oil exports rose in September to their highest level since the outbreak of the war in February, despite the Houthi attacks on Red Sea ports and infrastructure. (Al Jazeera)

APEC China 2026 Chile–Philippines relations The Philippines and Chile sign a free trade agreement as part of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, marking the former's first such agreement with a Latin American country. (Philippine Daily Inquirer)

China–Russia relations, China–United States relations, Russia–United States relations Chinese leader Xi Jinping, Russian president Vladimir Putin, and United States president Donald Trump hold their first trilateral meeting in Shenzhen during the APEC summit and issue a joint declaration addressing nuclear war, petroleum production, and United Nations reform. (AFP) (BBC News)
Pakistan–Qatar relations Pakistan and Qatar sign a memorandum of understanding on cooperation between their Federal Constabulary and Internal Security Force, respectively. (Al Jazeera)
Somalia–United Arab Emirates relations Somalia expels the ambassador of the United Arab Emirates, accusing the country of undermining Somalia's sovereignty. (AP)
Palestinians in Israeli custody An Israeli court extends the detention of Gaza's Kamal Edwan hospital director Hussam Abu Safiya by six months. (Al Jazeera)
Rohingya genocide case The International Court of Justice rules that Myanmar has committed genocide against the Rohingya people. (AFP)

Corruption in Mongolia The State Great Khural accepts the resignation of Mongolian president Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh. The chamber's chairman, Sandagiin Byambatsogt, assumes the acting presidency until a new election is held within four months. (AP)
